title: WebP to JPG – Convert WebP Images Free, No Upload
description: Convert WebP pictures saved from websites to JPG in your browser, so they open in every app. Many at once, transparency on white. Free, nothing uploaded.
heading: Convert WebP to JPG
subtitle: Turn WebP pictures from the web into JPG that every app opens; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Pictures saved from websites often arrive as WebP, which some photo apps, printers and upload forms still refuse. Convert them to JPG here: choose the quality, add as many as you like, and transparent parts are placed on white. The conversion runs in your browser, so the pictures never leave your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your pictures are read and changed by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees them.

features.title: Opens everywhere
features.text: JPG works in every app, printer and upload form that turns WebP away.

features.title: Many at once
features.text: Add as many pictures as you like; one result downloads as a picture, several as one ZIP file.

stepsTitle: How to convert WebP to JPG

steps.title: Pick the quality
steps.text: 85 to 90 keeps them looking the same.

steps.title: Convert and download
steps.text: Click Convert and download the JPG, or a ZIP of all of them.

handles: Files: still WebP pictures, lossy or lossless.
Transparency: placed on a white background, because JPG has none.
Output: JPG at the quality you choose, at full size.
Batch: many pictures in one ZIP.
limits: Animated WebP files become a still picture of their first frame.
JPG has no transparency; use WebP to PNG through the image converter to keep it.
Very large pictures (above about 100 megapixels) are limited by your device's memory.

faq.question: Are my pictures uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your pictures are read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and are never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: Why do websites give me WebP pictures?
faq.answer: WebP files are smaller than JPG at the same look, so websites load faster. Your apps may just not read them yet.

faq.question: How do I keep the transparent background?
faq.answer: JPG can't store it. Convert to PNG in the image converter instead.

faq.question: Will the JPG be bigger?
faq.answer: Usually a little, because WebP compresses better. Choose a quality of about 80 to keep it close.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
